text: I moved into this community right as it opened and have lived here for three years and I've seen a lot of changes. I'm about to move out so I thought I would update my initial review from a one star to two stars. The main reason for the addition of one star is the maintenance crew. Those guys are all top-notch! I have lived in a lot of apartment communities and these guys have been the absolute best. Literally, if you need something, say one of the track lights are out or something, they will not only replace it within a reasonable timeframe, but while they're there, they'll also change your air filter or something else you might need. I've called them after hours and they've talked me through a simple repair issue. During the recent hurricane, I saw the main maintenance guy had stayed in the building. He was super courteous and told me if there was anything I needed, to come see him in the model apartment. He said if he wasn't there because he was out taking care of the property, to leave a note, and he will address any issues right away. Those guys are absolutely amazing! Some other "pros" to living in the community, the gym with the cold aromatherapy towel service and the general location. And that brings us to the "cons" of the community. First, we will start with the name and address. When I first signed my lease, the community was called Crescent Bayshore which I suppose was fine, but I wasn't what the "Crescent" meant. I guess we're on a bit of a Crescent, but then there's also a Crescent Westshore, so I'm not sure. Maybe the confusion was what sparked a renaming of the community to 2 Bayshore. Now, that has caused a lot of confusion as well since that is not the actual address. We are sandwiched between 100 Bayshore and 345 Bayshore. It should maybe be 200 Bayshore. I am not sure if the 2 is supposed to be directional. Anyway, the address is actually 101 W. Beach Pl. NONE of it makes any sense. Also, if you're paying Bayshore prices, you really should have a Bayshore address. Next "con" is the parking garage/security issues. The gates to the garage are often broken, so now visitors just flood in and take up tenant spots. Or, when the gates are actually working, people just come in behind you. They installed an extra "arm" to the gate but apparently someone kept ramming it and they stopped using it. At some point, the arm was just dangling in front of the gate. Once, a guy literally waited while I parked and checked my mail, then followed me in through the gate. I took my time, he probably waited about five minutes to get in. This is a serious safety issue. This guy luckily kept going once I parked but I could see that ending differently some night. We have had a bunch of folks who had their cars "keyed", particularly on the seventh floor for some odd reason. There have also been a ton of folks who have had their bikes stolen, even from the "bike room." They do not know who committed any of the crimes. For the amount of rent we pay, there should be cameras ALL OVER that parking garage, zoomed in. There aren't. Frankly, I'm not sure if there are any. If you walk around the garage, the majority of the cars parked there do NOT have the required decal on their car. They should tow or boot people who are not authorized to park there. I pay significant rent for a two bedroom on the fourth floor facing the water and often find myself parking on the eighth floor facing a dumpster because the garage is so full. There should be assigned parking. It's not that difficult. This was not a problem when I first moved in, but the complex was brand new. It only recently became full and now everyone's significant other and visitors are sneaking into the garage, not to mention vandals. They should rip down the gate and build a guard station at the base of the garage and hire a guard to ensure that everyone coming into the garage actually belongs there. During the summer, they hired TWO rent a cops for the pool, which was completely unnecessary. A garage guard IS necessary at this point. Instead of spending money on things that are necessary, the complex blew holes in the concrete of the garage around the mailroom and installed a window in the mailroom, also completely unnecessary. Last "con" is the noise. My apartment faces the water and therefore, the helipad at Tampa General Hospital. You don't realize it but if you're in building one, the helicopters are constantly landing on the helipad, particularly on nights and on weekends when presumably there are more traumatic emergency situations happening. If you're a light sleeper, this would not be ideal for you. Thankfully, I have insomnia and when I finally do get to sleep, I'm a pretty heavy sleeper. Also, there are a few neighbors who leave their dogs out on their porches or balconies. These dogs bark constantly. I have complained but nothing has been done. I would not recommend this community to you. The cons outweigh the pros.

text: We did a sea kayak tour on Santa Cruz island. We got the boat from Ventura. It's quite easy to find and plenty of parking. Arrive a little early so that you can complete forms. There are other kayak tours and campers and day hikers leaving from this spot so you have to find the right check in person. But that is no problem at all. The boat ride over is about an hour. If u get sea sick take some Dramamine before hand. There are snacks and drinks to buy on the boat. Once you arrive you head to the kayaks where they will go through a safety and education piece. Don't worry if you've never kayaked before there are all levels here. You can store your stuff in a big container while you kayak. Bring some water and maybe a snack for the kayak tour. Depending on the temp u may feel cold and they have jackets and bottoms u can borrow and wear as u will get very wet and inside the caves can be chilly. We did not feel we needed them and it was overcast when we were there. You'll kayak for a couple of hours. It's tiring! Be aware of this :) but so much fun. The caves are incredible and the guides are knowledgeable fun and safe. They will help you if you need it. One of our party got exhausted and one of the guides just towed them. When you get back you can then hike or snorkel. They provide wet suits and all the gear. There is nothing on the island, so bring food and water with you and a change of clothing, again if the temps are low u will want to have something warm to put on. I really enjoyed this trip it was probably one of the best kayak tours I've done.

text: We were so terribly excited to try Little Octopus, being huge fans of Otaku. We wondered how they'd do, with what we'd heard was an upscale mostly-vegan menu. We found out. Our reservation was for start of business on a Saturday, and they opened on time. There were already a few people waiting, which we found encouraging. The first impression was, sad to say, cheapness. The furnishings look hastily put together or purchased at downscale yard sales. The chairs are comfortable enough, but the high table stools need backs, especially if they want to encourage drinking and sitting in enough comfort to keep ordering. When I mentioned to my wife that the furniture looked like it was from Ikea, she said "No, Ikea looks nicer." The ceilings are black, high, with everything showing. That was an interesting style when it first surfaced in the 70's New York loft scene, but not any more. I'm sorry to say this because I really wanted to love the decor. But it's cold, unfriendly, LA-modern-circa-1987. Our waitress was annoying in that she kept forgetting everything, even though she'd written it down. When she first brought water (which was filtered and quite good by the way), I covered my glass and said "I'd like ice in it please", but as soon as my hand was removed, she poured the water anyway. About five minutes later, she remembered to bring the ice, in a teeny tiny glass. Fortunately, the hostess filled in the blanks, and she was marvelous. The waitress did improve over the course of the meal, so perhaps it was just a bad day. I would highly recommend the lemonade. It was fresh, tart, not too sweet, just delicious. The green gazpacho, which had been touted highly by a reviewer, was all right, but not fantastic. We did enjoy the fingerling potatoes with chimichurri sauce - not too much sauce, and the broccoli was a terrific addition. One previous reviewer noted that the dishes do not come out in the expected order, eg appetizers first, mains second. This is very Japanese, but also very annoying. When you're trying to eat a cold bowl of soup, and your hot main arrives almost immediately after you begin, it's annoying. The only solution we thought of would be to insist on ordering only appetizers, and when done, ordering mains. However, our waitress seemed to be in quite a rush to get the whole order in, so be forewarned. I was excited to try the tofu, likewise touted in several reviews, but was very disappointed. I'm a big tofu fan, but American tofu is all about tastelessness to begin wtih, so the sauce or seasoning is really important. This tofu was, in a word, boring. Two slabs, with forgettable seasoning (actually, tasteless and burnt). I'd never have known it was sumac, which I've had before with tofu overseas and which can be delicious. It became more edible when I smeared it with the charred eggplant puree, but that was so salty it became uncomfortable, and I wound up not eating most of it. My wife had something else for her main which was so forgettable that neither of us can remember what it was, even after looking at the on line menu. Another criticism - the music was LOUD. I don't mean loud, I mean LOUD. That would have been fine at night, with a bar crowd, but at 11 o'clock in the morning it was really annoying. To be fair, they turned it down when several tables complained, but it was also uneven. Maybe they made their own mix tape and forget to level the volume on it? I don't know, but it was annoying. We were disappointed enough in the food that we didn't bother trying the desserts. In fact, we were glad to leave. Again, we had very high hopes, but we wouldn't bother trying this again. They were off to a rocky start, from what I can garner from the reviews, and perhaps the owner(s) are just stretched too thin at this point. I am finding, on this trip, that Nashville's new restaurants in general are over-hyped, or perhaps mostly attended by people who are not good cooks themselves and haven't eaten in many great restaurants. The city's foodies still seem to be playing catch-up with major cities like LA and New York, or Chicago or Philadelphia. I'd give a lot to be able to visit a regular old-fashioned diner here, if everyone is being so "adventurous", or a really great Italian restaurant (please don't send me to Mama Mia's, they're uneven at best.) I'm thrilled at the preponderance of local farmer's markets, local dishes, organic foods - and curious to try Avo and Two-Ten Jack next trip - but in general, this is still not a great food town. Sadly. I'm just hoping the "new" Otaku will be as good as the old!!!

text: In the past year a lot has changed at Sabor for Christian Mena and Lino Oliviera, the proprietors of this downtown Edmonton restaurant. Sabor has been renamed and rebranded, their third restaurant Urbano Pizza Co. has opened next door, and Sabor has become 100% Ocean Wise approved. That's a big list of accomplishments for one year, but the Ocean Wise certification is one of the most exciting for their annual seafood festival. I had the pleasure of attending the kick off to this year's Seafood Festival to preview some of Chef Lino's new dishes. The night started off with a bang with the Sabor Caesar Shot: a Malpeque oyster topped with sturgeon caviar and served with a Caesar shot featuring Eau Claire Three Point Vodka. I love that Sabor chose to feature Eau Claire Distillery - as Alberta's first craft distillery, their spirits are sure to impress if you haven't tried them yet! Each table was offered a Pinchos Board, featuring some of the items available on the menu at Bodega Tapas & Wine, to kick off the evening. Pinchos, which are related to tapas, differ such that pinchos are often presented spiked with toothpicks. In Spanish culture, the toothpicks serve as a method of picking up your food, but also as a way to charge you for how much you've eaten. Luckily Sabor doesn't charge based on toothpick count, because I would have had to shell out a lot of money! Our board for the evening featured Sabor's Aceitonas (house marinated olives, $5), octopus and mussel salad ($6, pictured above), crab fritters, seared scallops on pork belly, and snails in red wine with chorizo. The scallops and pork belly were a hit at our table, with the crispy crab fritters a close second. Olives, octopus and snail are such polarizing dishes to begin with, so I found that at our table there was not much in-between, you either liked the dish or you didn't. Our second starter for the evening was Chef Lino's play on Fish and Chips, featuring deep fried lake smelt and piri piri spiced chips. The fish were battered and fried to have a crisp coating, and the piri piri chips had a light seasoning to them. Fair warning though, the lake smelt are deep fried whole, so you chew on the small, edible bones with each bite. Unfortunately the fish and chips are not on the Seafood Festival menu, but Chef Lino will be featuring them once in a while throughout August. Next up was the beautiful Crudo Con Pebre ($24), featuring fresh Red Spring Salmon, Ahi Tuna, BC Coast Halibut, and BC Scallops. The raw seafood was topped with a simple combination of diced tomato, onion, garlic, cilantro, olive oil, and lemon which allowed the natural sweetness of each component to shine through. If you're a sashimi fan, this dish is for you. The following course was a Sardine Flatbread, paying tribute to Urbano Pizza Co. next door. The flatbread was light and covered in a briny onion and anchovy spread that I could not stop eating. Combined with the black olives and portions of sardines, I quite enjoyed this course for the evening. Entrees that evening kicked off with Grilled Humboldt Squid & Prawns ($18) on a bed of chorizo and white bean puree. This squid, otherwise known as the Red Devil, was cooked until soft and very easy to chew. I personally prefer my squid with more bite and chew (like most Asians!), so this dish may not be for everyone. What I really did enjoy though was the bean puree - rich, creamy, and with a kick of heat from the chorizo! Despite having tried a wide variety of tasty seafood dishes, the star of the evening for me was the Bacon Wrapped Sturgeon on Puttanesca Sauce ($32). Sturgeon flesh is quite under-appreciated given that the prized caviar is what most people are after. It was great to see this fish as the star of the plate, and the firmer texture made for a substantial protein.There was smokiness from the bacon, salt and acidity from the sauce, and natural sweetness from the fish to bring everything together. To finish off our family style meal everyone was treated to Mama Margarita's Pudim Flan. This flan is one of Chef Lino's favourite desserts made by his mother, and she finally caved and gave him the recipe. This Portuguese custard is creamy and sweet, and you can taste the richness of the eggs. Word on the street is that this custard is soon to become a gelato flavour at Urbano! While Sabor serves up seafood on their menu throughout the year, the best time to enjoy all that the restaurant has to offer is during the seafood festival. If you can't decide on a specific dish, Chef Lino is also offering off menu family-style dining at $55/person. It's great value and fun for the whole table! The seafood is fresh, the dishes are inventive, and best of all, everything is 100% Ocean Wise. What's stopping you?

text: OK, so visiting from out of town, and had already been eating minimally simple (i.e. my first love goes to tacos!), so thought I'd better try something with a local vibe. So from my experience, what this place really is is a coffeehouse/restaurant hybrid - which might work well in some ways, but not necessarily great in others. Because of the ambiguity, it's not clear whether or not their process' are synched. You walk in and it looks like a restaurant, because it's crowded with people and tables with plates of food. There is no hostess, or obvious sign directing you where to go. I looked up, and there was a sign on the ceiling towards the back saying, "Form line here". It LOOKS completely like a coffee/dessert counter, yet I'm still confused because, "is this where I order the food, also?" I just assumed, YES, but only after feeling dazed and confused for a few minutes. Note that the line snakes out to the back door, and the wait to get to the cashier was a good 20 min - and this was the lunch crowd going strong at 1:30p! I ordered the "Sweet Potato French Toast" at $11 - caramel, pecans, maple syrup, and whipped cream ...and also the Bulldog (espresso added to drip coffee). They give me a pager to pick up the coffee, and a tag to get the food delivered to you. Coffee was just OK; prob good to some people, but coffee, like alcohol, is a pretty personal thing, and twasn't my style - their drip brew was on the fruity side, and I can't stand fruity coffee. The french toast arrived, and even though I didn't know what to expect when they call it "sweet potato french toast", I assumed that it would be EXACTLY what they called it, which is "french toast", but it wasn't french toast in my dictionary. What it really was, was "sweet potato bread" as a quick bread (similar to zucchini, carrot, or banana bread loaves) with syrup on top. It was not a good combination to me, and kind of a gut bomber. Not what I was expecting, nor wanting, and should be the kind of thing that they sell behind the counter with their cakes. The name surely does imply that it's bread dipped in egg, and fried, traditional to what you normally get elsewhere. I am bummed that I paid money for disappointment.

text: So much to like, but yet so underwhelmed. I'd been eyeing Centro for a while with their appealing cocktail list and menu. The space is small, but they do their best to create a welcoming space with a mixture of small tables and pub style tables along with an attractive patio space in the back. The small space is opened up with rollup glass garage style doors. The interior is generally minimalist with brick, hard surfaces, and dark colors and a large bar/open kitchen space. The kitchen is certainly a centerpiece/show space with busy attractive staff hustling out food and drinks, the loud club type music adds to the "cool" factor of this restaurant. The drinks come out quickly and look well crafted. Flavors didn't live up to the descriptions or appearance, and were surprisingly bland. (Pims cup and Pisco sour, both fancy dressed up versions but both bland and watery compared to their classic renditions). The food was a mixed bag. We ordered quite a lot. Bread and Spread $5, Red quinoa falafel $6, Thai sticky ribs $8, beet salad $6, pulpo a la plancha $14, bread pudding waffle $8 ala mode $3. A breakdown on each dish: The bread and spread was supposed to be warm local bread and the daily spread was some sort of boiled down grapes and a few slices of compound butter. The bread was not warmed, nor was it fresh. It tasted at least a few days old and very dry and hard. It was a deck of cards sized section of some sort of olive bread and two leaves of a Pan d'Epi. The grape compote was ok, kind of like a halfway jam in a tiny 2 oz ramekin, the compound butter was nice. The falafel were good. I little mealy/mushy inside but tasted as expected. 3 cotton ball sized falafels served in a bowl with a dollop of yogurt and some thinly shredded veggies like cabbage. The ribs were 2 bones of extremely gamey pork deep fried and doused with fish sauce and a ton of sweet chili sauce that tastes exactly like the stuff you get in a bottle. I think it was served on top of a few thin slices of pickled carrot. The beet salad was a lovely composition of red and yellow beets, sliced grapes, queso fresco and a pair of snap peas arranged with dollops of yogurt and some herbal drizzle. This was the one dish we loved. Pulpo a la plancha was likely the most disappointing. It was two finger sized tentacles of extremely salty octopus with 2 thin drizzles of sauce and a grilled lemon slice. Octopus is not an expensive ingredient and the preparation of this dish was not complicated so I'm not sure what warranted the $14 price tag for this three bite dish. It was under the "dinner" plates and while I understand this is a small plate concept, I still expected it to be more than 2oz of food. The bread pudding waffle literally looked like vomit. The bananas foster caramel was a mealy looking beige smear and blob. The flavor was vaguely sweet and ripe bananas but no distinctive rum or brownsugar and spice that is indicative of banana foster. The gelato a la mode was thin in flavor and a bit icy, not really a rich dense gelato texture. so yeah, out of $70 of food and drink we were excited by one $5 dish. Half the items might have garnered more approval at a much lower price point, and the other half I wouldn't eat for free. But at least we felt hip while doing it. ha. I would like to say that the look/feel/staffing/and even the logo are all very nice and trendy in a good way. Even with my lack of enthusiasm for the food/drink, I think this place will still appeal to many for the overall cool factor and good service.

text: Cutting to the chase .... I LOVE DEL FRISCO'S Having dined at the del friscos double eagle steakhouse in NYC, i was very eager to give this one a try since it 1st opened in November. We were encouraged by our hostess & waitress on numerous occasions to check out the upstairs which had a cool roof top bar and even found a few booths for dining. The ceiling even had heat lamps which was a nice touch since it was a little cool outside. The place is a little on the pricey side but its just about what you would expect to pay when eating at one of the higher end restaurants in Tampa. We will def be coming back to experience the roof top bar for seconds and experience Del Friscos nightlife as it had some pretty nice views! We actually walked in around 9pm so we avoided the big crowds & was able to immediately land a prime spot right by the bar. Our server was very nice & immediately catered to us. Thankfully upon ordering, our food came out in a jiffy which was greatly appreciated since we were both starving beyond belief. I ordered an old fashioned which was good but was a little disappointed that most of the liquor selection at the bar was normal and nothing out of the ordinary. They did have a few interesting in house creations, as the misses ordered a "Kilt Lifter" which she enjoyed but i guess i expected more out of my cocktail. We ordered the truffled Mac & cheese and by far this was the BEST i have had yet. Although the portion was a little on the small side, each scoop from the dish was ultra creamy and it was just fun to see the cheese melting off the macaroni from every scoop. But what we loved most was the crisp that each bite had from the bread crumbs (?) sprinkled across the top. This should be a MUST order with EVERY meal!!! I ordered the Shaved Prime Steak Sandwich which was basically a nother name for a french dip sandwich. It came with a side of horseradish, ketchup, au jus dip, and a side of sweet potato fries. Sandwich was EXCELLENT and the bread came out slightly toasty. I've never had a french dip sandwich before but if they all taste like this then im ordering this EVERYTIME! I'm still dreaming about this sandwich (as i type!) as this was clearly one of the best things i have enjoyed in quite sometime! It had a little label next to it on the menu as a house special which was what drew me to it and im so glad that i did ! The misses ordered the Chicken Alfredo that was also splended and smelled amazing. Very creamy and paired well with the past and spinach. The portion was a nice size & I was able to take home half for lunch the next day and my co-workers were even wondering what smelled so good. Def a fan and soon to becoming one of my most favorite upscale restaurants in Tampa !

text: Went last year, had a great time. They dropped the ball in multiple ways this year, and based on our experience, I don't think we're going back. We arrived right around the start time, and it took over an hour to get in. The line stretched about a block down Cabrillo, then through multiple crowd management loops outside the gate. Once we got in, there was another long line to pick up the drinking glasses, which didn't move at all for a good long while. Turns out that they'd managed to run out of their special commemorative glasses about an hour into the festival. (Did they just give the early attendees a dozen glasses each? You'd think they'd know precisely how many they were going to need, based on the number of tickets sold.) The harried-looking staff rustled up styrofoam coffee cups and plastic shot glasses after another lengthy wait. They later ran out of those as well. Most of the attending breweries seemed to have brought their "C" game, too. A number were pouring half-inch samples by the time we finally made it in, with 2+ hours to go in the event. By 2 pm, multiple breweries had stopped pouring altogether. Several of the breweries advertised on the festival site were nowhere to be found. Nearly everyone seemed to bring their least interesting beers, and I was honestly sick of middle-of-the-road pale ales by the time we completed our circuit. Yeah, many beer festivals have that problem to a degree, but most manage to get at least a few more interesting beers into the mix. I think the only dark beer I found anywhere was Stone Smoked Porter, which I love, but... come on. The lineup was heavy on the usual suspects (the standard regional brewers, a few macros, and the largest number of wine coolers/alcopops/booze-for-people-who-don't-drink-booze I've ever encountered at a beer festival). Brews at the Beach is one of the lower-priced beer festivals in SB County, but it's honestly not worth the money for what you get. Next time I'll get a few friends together, raid Keg & Bottle, and have a way better time day-drinking in a backyard.

text: I read 5 negative reviews before we took our dog here but brushed them off. I realize every business has a few unhappy customers. But after our experience, now referring back to those reviews they are eerily similar to what my wife and I experienced. We went to check out the kennel 1st before booking w/ them. The grounds seemed well kept w/ many tall fences. Upon our visit we asked if the dogs can get over the fences. Shawna who I think is the manager laughed and shook her head no as if that was a silly question. She assured us that wouldn't happen. My wife explained that she gets nervous leaving him at new places. I would think a dog kennel would be sensitive to that. Once we booked with them & discussed pricing we were told how much it would be per day. We were asked if we wanted him fed once or twice a day. We requested twice a day b/c that's his normal eating routine. They told us 2 feedings a day would be an extra $2/day. We happily agreed to that. We dropped him off & left him in their care. We called the 1st day to check in and were told he was fine. The 2nd day we called & spoke with Shawna. She seemed annoyed. She said "I'm mad at him." That was just weird in and of itself. We asked why and she said "he climbed a fence." My heart dropped. She didn't elaborate. There was a long pause as if we were supposed to guess what happened. My wife and I thought that he got out and was MIA. We had to ask if he was ok. She didn't offer that info. She answered "yea he's ok." But again didn't elaborate. It took us prying for info to find out he jumped over a tiny fence that was inside a larger fence b/c he was trying to get to a group of dogs to play with. After we were finally told what happened which didn't seem that bad she told us that there may be extra charges. We asked why and she said "because we hadn't anticipated him being such a problem." She implied that b/c our dog jumped over a small fence he was a "problem" and that it could be $5 a day more. The issue wasn't the money. $5 more a day just seems punitive. It was the way we were talked to/the fact that she scared us w/out assuring us he was ok. Instead we were told our dog was a problem and we would maybe have to pay more. Why would you tell us that our dog is a problem when we are 2,000 miles away and can't do anything? The next day I decided to call the owner hoping for some clarity. I spoke with Natalie, the owner, who was slightly reassuring but I still felt uneasy after I spoke with her. She apologized for Shawna's insensitivity but stood her ground on the possible extra charges. Nobody disclosed to us that if he jumps over a fence therefore being deemed a "problem" there would be a fee. There should be at least something on their website that states that. Instead they don't disclose this and then if your dog does in fact do this, they make the owner feel awful. We came back to Tucson eager to get our dog but had to wait until 5pm because you can only pick up your dog between 5pm and 8pm. Nobody is there if you come before 5. This raises a red flag. Where is the staff during those hours? Dogs are completely unattended? What if something happened? A dog fight or God forbid a fire? We picked our dog up and when we walked in Natalie was there. She was rude & unprofessional. She asked us how many times a day THEY fed him. Seriously? They needed me to tell them how many times they fed my dog while in their care? We were informed that he was fed only once a day even though we asked for twice a day. She then implied that our dog needed discipline classes. He's a puppy! We brought him there to have fun and play! We didn't bring him there to win some kind of best in show award and be judged as owners. When I told her he did have some classes and started to explain that they didn't work, she cut us off and said "perhaps because mommy coddles him too much?" Excuse me? I was trying to explain before she rudely cut me off that the training didn't work b/c the instructor cancelled so often w/out rescheduling. It was inconsistent. If Kennel Nirvana only wants Cesar Millan disciples, then specify that. Don't act like all dogs are welcome if they aren't. We wrote a check for $75 (we had already paid a $50 deposit) making the total $125 for 5 days. Upon writing the check she actually said "tips are appreciated." If anything money should have been taken off our bill for how we were treated & for the night we laid awake in bed worried. Our dog also lost 5 pounds while there. Maybe b/c he wasn't fed properly! He was inside for most of the time so I know he didn't lose weight from just playing. I get the sense that they don't really care about the well being of the dogs staying at their kennel or how the owners feel. I think they are a tired, understaffed, older staff who have been doing this for a long time and are possibly burnt out. Well then close up shop if you can no longer provide quality care to your customers and treat the dogs the way they deserve.

text: UPDATED REVIEW Talk about a location that just keeps getting better with age; in the 9 months since my first review the Lambertville OwowCow has seen a marked improvement in staff, an increase in options, and the ever-high-quality ice cream I have come to know and love is still amazing. PROS The ice cream is the reason you come to OwowCow. It is thick, rich, and flavorful. There is always a rotating blend of wonderful and creative flavors, ranging from traditional (three variants on vanilla and the classic "I Hate Chocolate" - the best chocolate ice cream you may ever taste) to unique, fruity, and floral. Even better, unlike some ice cream places I have been, they have no problem with you taking your time to decide - offering samples of as many flavors as you would like and taking the time to explain what is unique about the flavors. The serving sizes here are VERY generous. In a regular cup (my normal order) you get two giant scoops (of one or two flavors). Even for someone who loves ice cream and can eat a lot, I am always completely satisfied. They have a lot of other options besides just ice cream in a cup (although I rarely can bring myself to stray from my favorite). From shakes and floats (made with local sodas) to hand-made ice cream sandwiches (with cookies from a local baker), there is always something new to try. Also, during holidays they often have specialty cakes and pies available for order. We got their pumpkin ice cream pie over Thanksgiving - it was stunning! The staff are almost all very welcoming and friendly. When it is really busy, sometimes the staff are a little less chipper - but I would be too! It is nice to be welcomed with a smile. The location and ambiance is great. There are almost always enough seats if you want to stay and enjoy your deliciousness, the art on the walls is inviting, and it is close enough to downtown Lambertville that you can (if the weather is nice) walk downtown and enjoy the shops and then get ice cream on your way back to your car. CONS It is true that they are not the cheapest option in the world (a regular ice cream is $4.20), but they are in line with other places in the area of similar quality (and you get more bang for your buck compared to a high-end place like the Bent Spoon in Princeton). For me, the price isn't out of line, but we can't afford to come here every day either. And that's ok both for my wallet and my health. On a busy day parking can be tough, but usually workable. OVERALL OwowCow has become my favorite ice cream place in the whole region; enough so that my family and I will often make the half-hour or so drive from Princeton just for ice cream. All you really need to know is that the ice cream is fresh and delicious. Still on the fence? Come give it a try for yourself!

text: I came to Eddie Vs with a group of 6 for a special occasion, and I must say, it is the perfect place for a celebration. We were seated as soon as we arrived, even though the restaurant was pretty busy (7pm on a Friday evening). The server extensively explained the specials of the day, and after describing the fish of the day, even told us what the market price was that day. I really appreciated this because asking what the market price is can be somewhat awkward, don't you think? Our group started by sharing a couple appetizers. We ordered the Point Judith Calamari, and the pot stickers ( filled with shrimp and pork).. Both were consumed rapidly and we fought over the last few pieces. I ordered the shrimp and crab chopped salad for my meal and it was great. I give it 4.5 stars. Other members of my party ordered the florida grouper, the north atlantic lemon sole, and the jumbo gulf shrimp from the seafood side, and a couple filet mignons as well. I tasted most dishes, and I think the Lemon Sole wins for the night. It was moist and flavorful and I loved the parmesan topping. We also made it a point to try several different side dishes. We got the Crab Fried Rice (5 stars!), the sautéed sweet corn (best corn I've had at a fancy steakhouse ever) and thr truffled mac n cheese (duh). If you are going to pick just one side (I wouldn't recommend just picking one - go all out), I would suggest the crab fried rice. It was a crowd favorite. Since it was a special occasion, the waiter also sent over a "hot" banana's foster dessert that was DELICIOUS. Oh, it was also on fire when it was delivered to the table, and we all enjoyed the little presentation. The banana's foster cake was topped with a butter pecan icecream that went perfectly with the cake and fresh bananas. I always appreciate when a restaurant takes special celebrations into consideration, so this was the perfect end to my Eddie V's experience.

The chilli cheese fries were pretty delicious, also. The fries were layered with generous portions of chilli and cheese. The Cuban sandwich was out of this world good! They cut it lengthwise, and serve it with a mojo dipping sauce which softens the bread just right. I recommend getting the mojo sauce spicy. Their take on a Cubana is the best I've had in the Bay Area (so far). It's loaded with generous portions of meats, dabbed with the right amounts of pickles & mustard, and a fairly large sandwich for a decent price. I will go back just for the Cuban, but all the food is really good here. The dining area is not big, but not real small either. text: Burgers are my favorite "bad" meal - the kind of thing I crave when hungover or when I haven't eaten all day and want to get all my calories at one sitting. So I was invited to the friends and family soft opening and agreed immediately. We got there and were seated immediately. Ambiance is casual but modern and slick and new. Big bar in the middle of the room and tables all around. If you were wondering about the menu, well, they have all types of burgers. Yes, as the name says, it is all about burgers so if you don't like that you probably shouldn't go. They do have a turkey burger option, some standard burgers, lamb burger, "chorizo" burger, etc and so forth. And they have sides such as fries cooked in beef fat (um...YESSSS), onion rings, etc. Oh and they also have booze, which is my favorite. Drinks were good cocktail creations and there were choices for whatever liquor you prefer. They also have beer and such. And probably Coke and water too but...boring. Given my first trip to FLIP in Birmingham I steered away from the chorizo burger. Not that it isn't good, but that it isn't CHORIZO. To me, that implies a burger either mixed with or totally made out of CHORIZO which is SAUSAGE. This is PORK with CHORIZO SPICES. There's a big difference. Just FYI. So this time I went with the lamb burger because I can totally get into any Mediterranean flavors. The burger was big and well spiced and flavorful. The fries were good as only fries cooked in beef fat can be...if they were just a smidgen skinnier I'd be putting these on my best French Fries list. Service was friendly and excited if a bit disjointed but it was a soft opening so overall was impressed. Our waitress was so pumped about everything on the menu and seemed excited to be working there so it was really fun and refreshing. Definitely give this place a try when you are craving a burger. I know I will since it is not too far from my house and there are so many other burgers to try on the menu!

It's a great addition to the park for swimming and exercising. JB also has an amphitheater for concerts, festivals and carnivals. The whole park sits alongside the Mississippi River on lovely bluffs. There are great scenic views and plenty of picnic tables, covered pavilions and park benches. I haven't even started on all the historical features of this park including a WWII museum, Civil War artifacts and other historical areas. Of course all of this rests alongside the Jefferson Barracks National Cemetery which is a place of beauty, sacrifice and inspiration. If you haven't been to Jefferson Barracks, or JB as the locals refer to it, you're missing out on one of St. Louis' true gems.

The first course was the side salad, which came with homemade honey mustard dressing. The dressing itself had a nice balance between a sweet honey and mustard flavor. So far, so good. Then, the main dish was delivered. It was hard to tell from the photo, but the portion size was more than adequate. The pork tenderloin itself was cooked perfectly and had a great texture. The first time I went, the baked pecorino was taking a bit longer than usual to come out so she just gave it to us on the house. Five minutes later, out comes the cake, also on the house! The second time I went, they gave us ricotta on the house as well. So considerate, and it made the dining experience all the better! ATMOSPHERE: Amis has a well-lit, airy, bright atmosphere. There are beautiful lamps made of little red bottles of cordial. text: My dreams were crushed when I dined here last night. The delectable scent of food wafting from The Southern since its inception has enticed me for years when I would drive through downtown Nashville. The menu looks incredible, they offer free valet parking, so who wouldn't want to try this popular and trendy spot for a special occasion? I knew I would dine here eventually! And I finally did! You should make reservations two weeks in advance or you probably won't get in. So I did just that, surprising my wife for her birthday. We ordered what seemed like a scrumptious array of food, and there isn't much in this world I enjoy more than exquisite food!!! Right off the bat, I noticed the bread was pretty good but not outstanding. The oysters were very good but my favorite seafood dish, Oysters Rockefeller, was not even on the menu. The macaroni and cheese and mashed potatoes were very good. The Caesar salad had great moments of shaved Parmesan and salty meat followed by bitter pieces of lettuce. But here was the major let down! The word "steak" is actually part of the restaurant's title so one would think that would be a safe bet. And yet the T-bone steak, something this place is known for, was surprisingly bland and definitely undercooked (somehow medium became rare). Their delicious homemade seasoning that sits on every table helped salvage the meat to some extent. But I've had far better steaks for far less than $54!!! There were some intriguing flavors throughout the meal. And for half the price, I probably would have given it four stars. But I just can't see myself ever returning to this restaurant to pay $120, for two, for a meal that was only slightly superior to a Logan's Roadhouse outing for less than half that amount! It's not that the food was terrible (except the disappointing steak). It's the fact that the exorbitant prices simply aren't worth what you get in return. You don't get your money's worth here! P.S. When I pay over $100 for a meal in New York or Los Angeles, I feel like I'm dining in heaven! After years of anticipation, The Southern didn't even come close to that feeling. I judge the merit of all steaks by Wolf Lodge Inn in Idaho, the best in the world, and this steak didn't even come close.

My dog recovered within a week, and unfortunately needed to make one more return trip for an antibiotic, but the team here called almost daily to see how he was progressing and asked if we needed anything. I truly felt they cared for my dog's - and my - comfort. My husband and I found out we were being transferred to Europe and couldn't take our dog with us immediately, so he needed to make a month stop over with my parents in the summer of 2015. There is extensive paperwork and exams required when traveling overseas with a dog, and West Chester Medical Clinic was where we knew wanted to take our dog to handle his care while he was in Philly. Again, the service here was truly fabulous. They walked us through every step required for the paperwork, administered the vaccines with the utmost care, and ensured he was fully prepared to travel. Dr. Gonzales is a gem of a vet - and his tech team is equally as amazing. They even called my parents after we traveled to Germany to make sure he made it OK! WOW! I only wish I loved my regular vet in Seattle as much as I love this clinic - and I only hope we can find a vet as wonderful here in Berlin - otherwise I may have to fly him back just for care with this clinic.

I am providing this feedback not as an attack, but in the hopes that they will take it upon themselves to do this and to ENSURE that no one ever leaves their store with a subohm tank or a RDA without knowing ohms law and exactly what batteries are safe to use with these setups. In this store or any other, do NOT buy an Aspire Atlantis tank or Kanger Sub Tank without reading about them first, same for trying to build subohm coils. It is not ok to use a "protected" battery with these. You NEED a IMR battery (safer chemistry vs protected) that is high drain, high amp. Look for a video of a battery "venting" and learn that anything else is UNSAFE. I believe all vape shops should be fully educated on this topic and those tanks should come with big warning labels on them. They can be safe and AWESOME with proper batteries. Otherwise, you are putting a pipebomb in your hand and face. If i misunderstood the knowledge level, i apologize, but its not ok to be unclear with customers on this topic. text: Mama's is closed and you're craving falafel. What's a philly girl to do? Check Yelp naturally. I found this place which is just a stones throw away from East Passyunk Ave after trying and disliking other Mediterranean joints in the area. Mazza is under new ownership by a great Philadelphian named Larry who is using a mix of his family's own recipes and the old owners recipes. Let me tell you, it works. My goodness, this falafel gives mama's a run for its money. Not only that, this place makes a MEAN hummus. This isn't dizengoff-esque hummus that's more on the creamy side, this is the thick stuff, perfect for stuffing a pita with. My Israeli fiancée gave this place one big fat stamp of approval. The stuffed grape leaves were served warm and were delicious and Larry's grandmother's baklava was excellent as well. My only complaints? The price is a little high for a take out joint, but maybe only a dollar or so more than what I'd like to spend. Also, the place isn't the quickest. We just walked in and ordered and had to wait about 15-20 min but it seems like they have a solid delivery business that makes the place busy even though we didn't see a lot of foot traffic coming in. Also, don't get the whole wheat pitas, they are more like a wrap than the fluffy white pitas. Mazza is definitely a south philly hole in the wall, in a great neighborhood, that's worth giving another try if you haven't been in the last 6 months since Larry took over. We will definitely be coming back.

text: I'm always a fan of Chinese food that doesn't make me feel like crap after. I'm an even bigger fan of Chinese food when a great portion of the menu isn't fried. Xi'an is pretty dang good. I've been there three times now and it has never disappointed. The portions are large and the prices are reasonable. Definitely get the Biang Biang Noodles w/ Ginger Scallion Sauce. It was my cure for the New Years hangover (but I've gotten it every time I go). The noodles are perfectly cooked and just the right amount of spicy/slipperyness. The Xi'an Liang Pi noodles are ranked just behind the Biang Biang. They are light and almost sour. It says two chilis on the menu, but the spice isn't there. The noodles themselves aren't quite as good as the Hand Drawn Noodle House, but I still dig it. If you like stir-fried eggplant, you HAVE to get the eggplant in garlic sauce. The eggplant is perfectly cooked and the brown garlic spicy sauce is fantastic. It can get very busy, so you might expect a wait, even at 2 pm on a Saturday. But it's worth it.

text: I have been training in 24Hour SB for 9 months and it has been the best gym I've ever trained in. He is encouraging and motivating, and he always makes sure to push your mind and body enough to realize how far you can get with hard work and a little more patience. As being a big traveler, a two and half hour flight could knock my back out completely, and I could have extreme back pain for weeks. After training with Matt, on my way home, which is a twelve hour flight, I walked out like I've never had a back problem ever in my life. It was amazing. Matt, taught me how I should take care of every single part of my body, how I can prevent injuries, what it means if I have pain in a particular bodypart and what to do to stop it, and make my weaknesses my strength. Matt, is not only an amazing trainer but also, a great friend who has influenced me for the better in many areas of my life than fitness. Anyone who wants to get a PT there is no right person than Matt. He believes in you and he wants you to be the best version of yourself. text: If you have an item on your menu that boasts "Sriacha cream cheese" it's a fair bet you know what you are doing. The folks at Subito clearly do. Tucked away on Virginia Street, this soup and sandwich takeaway spot adds an element of spice to the drab quick lunch scene in downtown Indy. The Georgetown was a delight, on the beautiful house baked ciabatta was spread the aforementioned Sriacha cream cheese accompanied by sautéed onions and a sizable amount of pastrami. It was a revelation. Take a look at the menu, however, and you'll see that their passion is soup. I had the Italian wedding and it was flush with chunks of sausage and speckled with couscous. It was somehow better than the sandwich, which I didn't think was possible. Need more incentive to visit? Look at the bonkers rotating soup menu. Roasted red pepper and sweet potato? Looks like I'll be there on 10/6. Butternut squash prosciutto? October 14th, baby. Smoked Salmon Chowder?! October 23rd! It's hard to go wrong with any selection, though, as when you craft food with passion, rarely do you worry about the outcome.

text: This place was a nice surprise in a residential-seeming area of Havertown. You can't ever go wrong with being able to BYO (as long as you remember to bring your wine and/or beverage of choice). The restaurant is decorated tastfully inside and they had plenty of seating and were able to accomodate our somewhat large group of six and another nearby table of double the size, as well as a bunch of 2 and 4 tops. The only thing that was a little surprising was that their was only 1 bathroom, which didnt seem like enough for as many people were eating in the restaurant, but I didn't really run into too much of a line. Another thing I noticed was that it got really smoky in the restaurant while they were cooking. They had to keep the doors open to let some of the smoke out, so there must not be great ventilation in there. It wasn't too bothersome, but definitely noticeable. For dinner, I had the salmon entree, which was placed over potatoes and spinach, It was a large piece of salmon nicely seared and crunchy on the outside with a nice beurre blanc sauce on top and very reasonably priced for $25. My only complaint was that the almon was a bit overdone and dry. My fiancee had the surf and turf special, which was a tasty 6 oz filet with 3 shrimp over rissotto. However, for his entree, I thought the price was a little steep at $39 for a smallish steak and 3 shrimp, but it is BYOB so I guess you pay for being able to save on wine and liquor. Finally we had the brownie sundae. which was really cute and came in a wine glass with sprinkles definitely a good choice for kids and kids at heart. Finally, our server was very nice and helpful throughout the evening and didnt try to rush us out after we had been there for a while catching up with our friends, which was much appreciated. I would definitely give this place a try again if I'm in the area.

text: This is the first time Ive ever reviewed anything on Yelp the same day I visited a restaurant. text: The hotel itself is just fine. Great location. Nothing fancy, all the essentials. I will say that when we got here the shower hot water was running and would not shut off. That was fixed when we talked with the front desk. The restaurant/breakfast buffet which is doubletree is what is getting a one star rating. Normally I would not rate an entire hotel a one star just based on an experience with one part of the hotel, but I was so disturbed by the lack of friendliness, professionalism and helpfulness. I've worked in restaurants before and have put on large scale events, and never have I ever seen such a lazy group of people as well as people who just really have no business working with people. The first day here we tried to have breakfast but at 10:45am were told that they stopped serving already even though people were still getting food from the buffet. Breakfast was supposed to be served until 11am. Today when coming down to get the buffet at 10:30am. There were several people waiting and there were THIRTEEN tables of varying sizes available. Then we were told there would be a 15-20 minute wait. While waiting and watching the staff move as slow as molasses, a family complained about there being tables available and needing to eat before they get on a plane home. Then we watched as the hostess slowly walked to clean a table for them as slow as humanly possible. Then she sat the group. When we also said the same thing she went and cleaned off another table and sat us. A server overheard us complaining and stated that the reason there was such a wait was because all of the staff was lazy. He was the only friendly person who did seem to enjoy what he was doing. The food was cold and not that tasty but it was free. Except it wasn't, we recieved a bill for over $40 and they said that it was not free, but that only the continental breakfast was free. Apparently the two serving areas for the buffet were seperate (even though there was no sign and they were next to eachother). When we got the manager to speak with him, he was rude and unapologetic and seemed annoyed that he had to speak with customers and said that we would have to pay the full amount, We explained that the hostess and waitress asked if we had breakfast vouchers and when we said that we did they said to help ourselves to the buffet. We had to go to the front desk to have them waive any fees because the manager refused. They agreed that there was a mistake. When I tried to help improve their process and customer service by suggesting that they explain that to you when you are waiting to be seated and that they post signs designating the area the manager Dustin just said very rudely okay and then walked away. I can honestly say that these are the things that make me never want to stay at a Doubletree again. Providing friendly service and wanting to help people is clearly not apart of any training or requirement of staff. And I have never been at a restaurant with an issue where the manager flat out says we are wrong and doesn't try to help and make the situation better. And we were not wrong which is the most frustrating part. I think with better management this could change but when a manager is rude and clearly hates his job, the staff will follow suite. text: Dear God......where to start with this place!! We booked through Booking.com and their photos were completely misleading. Bottom line, "Run Away! Run Far, Run Fast from this place!" And may I remind you that this was Friday afternoon of Memorial Day weekend in New Orleans!! And there on the wall behind the front desk were two signs, one of which read "No Pimps, No Prostitutes, No Drug Dealers"!!! We were assigned a room that was completely around the back. But before we were given the keys, one of the desk clerks had to take a run to the room to make sure it was "OK". A few minutes later, she returned announcing that the room was "perfect". We found it odd that the front portion of the parking lot was chain-linked off to prevent anyone from driving to the back to the left of the building, since the fencing directly across from our room was completely knocked down, allowing anyone to enter or leave. 2. The room to the right of ours had its windows broken in, while the room to our left was missing its entire locking system, AND its toilet!! 3. The Family Inns also advertised a Continental breakfast each morning, but we came to discover that the Board Of Health had closed down the kitchen. Thus, no Continental breakfasts were provided. 4. We entered a room that had only two "double beds", NOT the king and the queen sized I had paid for and expected!! The carpeting was horribly filthy and the room smelled of something unidentifiable. The bathtub had cigarette burns and blood stains!! I'm pretty sure at least one hooker had bled out in the bathroom and a number of people woke up in the tub packed in ice with a kidney missing. There were also cigarette holes and burns on the bedspread!! 5. Sitting in a chair for a few moments before our having to make an appointment, a mouse ran out from under one of the beds, tried to get into one of the dresser drawers and then ran back under the bed!!! When getting down to see under the bed, we came to discover that the batting to the box spring was ripped and torn, making it a perfect way for mice to get in and out!!! 6. Needless to say, we weren't at all excited at the prospect of leaving our luggage there, but we had little choice at that point! 7. Empty fire extinguisher boxes dotted the area. When we arrived, the pool was filled with children, and yet, there were no cars in the parking lot to suggest that the kids belonged to anyone staying there, which led us to believe they were children from the surround neighborhoods. 8. Overall it was like being in Motel Hell for the night. None of us slept soundly, we seriously considered sleeping in shifts to make sure no one broke in while we were sleeping. 9. Also, minor I know, but the Wi-Fi only worked in the lobby....it didn't even show up as an option on my phone in the room. Because it was Memorial Day Weekend, we were unable to find affordable accommodations for the remainder of our stay. We ended up checking out the next morning. The "clerk" explained that he didn't know how to do refunds and that the manager would have to contact us when he came in later that afternoon. We left our name, address and phone number. Not surprisingly, no one contacted us. Calls were made and messages left but never any responses. I only wish I could post pictures here of the mess this place was. Lesson learned. Never using Booking.com again....EVER. They obviously never check out the locations of businesses they advertise, recommend.

text: Easily the highlight of our vacation was finding this tour company. Thanks Yelp! I knew that there was at least 3 or 4 tours we wanted to do and I knew most tour companies charge $20-$30 a person, per a tour, which means we would've been spending over $200 just on tours. This company touts "free" tours and encourages you to tip the tour guide at the end for "what you can afford or what you think the tour is worth". We ended up doing 3 tours... VOODOO TOUR with Robi: AWESOME 2 hour walking tour guided by Robi, a VooDoo priest with a real, vested interested in VooDoo and the history of New Orleans. This guy is the real deal. He is a descendent of slaves and lives on his family's original plantation. His grandmother was a VooDoo priestess and he knows everything there is to know about this religion. He is an excellent storyteller, extremely knowledgeable, encourages you to ask questions and pretty funny too. This tour will take you past Marie Laveau's house, to Congo Square, and a VooDoo temple. HIGHLY recommended. ST LOUIS CEMETERY with Kathy: Excellent tour of the oldest cemetery in New Orleans. Kathy was knowledgeable and passionate about New Orleans history and there was not a question she did not know the answer to. My only complaint about this tour was that our group was pretty large and Kathy's voice wasn't quite loud enough to carry, so I couldn't hear some of her stories and facts. As a tip, just know that the Catholic church has closed the cemetery's to tourists - the only way to get in is to be part of a guided group. So if you want to get into the cemetery's, be sure to sign up. FRENCH QUARTER with Andrew: Another excellent 2 hour walking tour that takes you on a full loop around the French Quarter. This guy knows his stuff. You'll hear the history of some of the 250 yr old restaurants in the area, stories about fires, Spanish rule, French rule, why buildings look as they do, and my absolutely favorite history lesson - the story of Baroness de Pontalba. Andrew will tell you which bars, restaurants to hit up and which to avoid, and will give you any other recommendations and information upon request. He will even give you book recommendations if there was a topic he covered that you want more info on. I've already looked up his book recommendation on the Baroness. "From here on, you have a local friend in New Orleans if you have any questions or need to find anything, just email me." Excellent tour. Overall, I think we "tipped" a little over $100 on all three tours. I was appalled when I saw one well-dressed lady give a tour guide two $1 bills, as I forked over $30. These tour guides are real experts and are working hard in the heat and humidity to show you a good time in their city. I would certainly say that's worth more than $2. OK, rant over - highly recommended tour company. Thank you Free Tours By Foot!

text: The Rusty Pelican is aptly named. Everything about this place is a bit rusty. The menu reads fine, if uninspired. The decor is dated and the staff is less than enthusiastic. It is spacious if you are looking to treat a large group to mediocre food and a nice view, the RP is your place. For me everything was just a bit off. The appetizers we ordered: artichokes, tomato mozzarella stack and calamari were all one thing too many or one thing too few. The baby artichokes looked delicious but they were entombed in breading and deep fried. The tomato stack was topped with a horrible balsamic dressing that tasted of horseradish, instead of a nice simple balsamic drizzle or reduction. I am a vegetarian and can't speak to the calamari, but I was with a group that usually cleans their plates and there was calamari left over. My dinner was salad (which came with the same horrible dressing) succotash, and risotto. The succotash was very good, flavors were fresh, vegetables cooked properly and seasoned well. The risotto was fair. It was creamy but lacked depth of flavor. Could have benefited from an herb and a squeeze of lemon. My co diners had fish and all seemed fine with their choices, no one raved about anything. We finished with dessert. An over-crusted key lime pie and a flaming crime brûlée. Key lime was ok, brulee was nicely done..cold and creamy underneath, nicely Carmelized. My only complaint is the run they douse it with to flambé it drained onto the fresh fruit making it inedible. All in all I'd say pass by the rusty pelican in search of something slightly less rusty.

I reviewed with her my conversation from the day before and what I was after. She proceeded to refute most of what I was told the day before about what I really needed for this fish. Not to mention, that she spent most of the time with a tone as if I was some kind of animal abuser by considering on the type of setup the manager from the day before suggested. My wife picked up on this right away and we both had a fairly uncomfortable feeling. The store had a display with a similar fish in it and was selling it as a 'package' for everything you would need to get started. I asked about that and was told by the employee that she would never keep a fish in that and we shouldn't either. At this point I couldn't get out of there fast enough. Since I knew what I wanted, we bought a fish, some food and gravel and got out of there. We headed straight to the nearest big box pet store (what I wanted to avoid) to get the tank and other accessories. I will say that the prices for similar items were cheaper at The Reef as compared to where we ended up. I'm hoping this is just an isolated bad experience with an employee (since my previous visit was fine) but it was likely uncomfortable enough for me not to go back. I will say that on both occasions, the store had a lot of customers.

text: We decided to stay here to save money... You definitely get what you pay for. The room itself was clean, no bedbugs, no issues with anything unsanitary, etc. And there's a gated pool with reasonably clean chairs. Extremely convenient to the interstate and around 10mins to get downtown. However: -The hotel provides you with two recommendations for taxis - Morerro and United. Do yourself a favor and look up Glenn's instead. (Kim was awesome!) -Regardless of what you reserve, the hotel has two options for rooms: a single king or a double full. And though the whole hotel claims to have three cots, all three were "taken" for the duration of our stay. -They claim to have laundry facilities, all of which were outside and most of which were out of order. -Each time any of us went downstairs, there was only one person working, regardless of how many people were waiting. Phones ringing like crazy, two or three people in line, you get the idea. Waited 15mins just to check in. -The surrounding area is extremely... Poor. Saw multiple people of questionable motive/quality. Closest grocery is Sav-A-Lot and has very limited selections. - The day we checked out, we noticed a "Crime Scene Clean-Up" van with people in clean-suits in and out of a room below us.. Still unsure of what happened there... - The free WiFi never worked. It was an available network, but out of the four of us, not one could get it to work. I've already been promised that next time we go, we will stay somewhere downtown. Transportation across the river is neither cheap nor convenient. (Even the ferry is $2 per person, per trip, with limited hours. When it's up and running.) The difference in what you would pay for the room across the river and what it will cost you to get there from here is pretty negligible. I would even say that you may save money (and definitely time) staying downtown.
label: NEG
